title: Compact-support projection map commutes with base change (finite rings and coefficient towers)
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X,Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism and let $v:Y'\to Y$ be any $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $X'=X\times_YY'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-base-change]. Choose a compactification $f=p\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ an open immersion and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $\overline X'=\overline X\times_YY'$, with projections $p':\overline X'\to Y'$ and $\bar u:\overline X'\to\overline X$, and $j':X'\hookrightarrow\overline X'$ the base change of $j$, so that $f'=p'\circ j'$. No flatness, smoothness or properness of $v$ is assumed.

Use one of the following two coefficient settings.

(i) A finite commutative ring $A$ with $\ell^rA=0$ for some $r\geq1$, and the ordinary, uncompleted, unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A)$ of module sheaves over the constant ring $A_T$ on the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with the derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_A$ [def-weil-derived-tensor], the derived inverse images $u^*$ (exact, termwise), derived direct images and their adjunctions $u^*\dashv Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and termwise extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero].

(ii) A finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ of varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], that is, of modules over the ring system $(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_{n\geq1}$ in the topos of inverse systems of sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Here inverse image is exact levelwise inverse image, direct images are the total right derived functors of levelwise direct image with their derived adjunctions, extension by zero is levelwise, and $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ is the derived tensor product over the ring system; no completed tensor product is used.

In either setting put $F_f=Rp_*j_!$ and $F_{f'}=Rp'_*j'_!$, and use the canonical pullback/tensor comparison $v^*(V\otimes^{\mathbf L}W)\cong v^*V\otimes^{\mathbf L}v^*W$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the pullback-composition isomorphisms. For $M$ on $X$ let
$$\beta_M:v^*F_fM\longrightarrow F_{f'}u^*M$$
be the compact-support exchange: the proper exchange $v^*Rp_*\to Rp'_*\bar u^*$ (the mate of $p'^*v^*\cong\bar u^*p^*$) at $j_!M$, followed by $Rp'_*$ of the extension-by-zero base-change isomorphism $\bar u^*j_!M\cong j'_!u^*M$. For $M$ on $X$ and $K$ on $Y$ let
$$\operatorname{PF}_f(M,K):F_fM\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow F_f(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f^*K)$$
be the projection map: the proper projection map of $p$ at $(j_!M,K)$ (the adjoint transpose under $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ of the counit $p^*Rp_*j_!M\to j_!M$ tensored with $1_{p^*K}$, after the pullback/tensor comparison), followed by $Rp_*$ of the extension-by-zero tensor isomorphism $j_!M\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*K\cong j_!(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*p^*K)$ and $j^*p^*\cong f^*$. In setting (i) these are the compactification composites of [def-exchange-projection] formed with the coefficient ring $A$; in setting (ii) they are the same composites formed in the inverse-system topos.

Then for all $M$ on $X$ and $K$ on $Y$ in these ambient derived categories one has, naturally in $M$ and $K$,
$$\beta_{M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f^*K}\circ v^*\operatorname{PF}_f(M,K)=\operatorname{PF}_{f'}(u^*M,v^*K)\circ(\beta_M\otimes1_{v^*K})$$
as maps $v^*F_fM\otimes^{\mathbf L}v^*K\to F_{f'}(u^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f'^*v^*K)$; here the source of the left side $v^*(F_fM\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ is identified with $v^*F_fM\otimes^{\mathbf L}v^*K$ by the pullback/tensor comparison, and its target $F_{f'}u^*(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f^*K)$ with $F_{f'}(u^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f'^*v^*K)$ by that comparison and $u^*f^*\cong f'^*v^*$. Consequently, whenever $\beta_M$, $\beta_{M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f^*K}$, $\operatorname{PF}_f(M,K)$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{f'}(u^*M,v^*K)$ are isomorphisms,
$$(\beta_M\otimes1_{v^*K})\circ v^*\operatorname{PF}_f(M,K)^{-1}\circ\beta_{M\otimes^{\mathbf L}f^*K}^{-1}=\operatorname{PF}_{f'}(u^*M,v^*K)^{-1}.$$

proof.text: Work uniformly in ringed topoi. In (i) use the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. In (ii), [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] identifies the category with modules over the ring object $(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_n$ in the inverse-system topos. A small site for this topos is the diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$; its sheaf equivalence carries this varying ring object as well. The scheme inverse images act levelwise, preserve this ring object, and their right adjoints are levelwise direct images: the usual adjunction bijection restricts to compatible families because its bijections are natural. Their derived adjunctions are exactly the ones stipulated in the item. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies the canonical uncompleted derived tensors and tensor comparisons in either case. It also gives K-flat representatives preserved by pullback. All subsequent equalities are in these ringed-topos derived categories. Write $G=v^*$, $H=\bar u^*$, $U=u^*$, $R=Rp_*$, $R'=Rp'_*$, and write $e:GR\to R'H$ for proper exchange. Let $b_M:Hj_!M\to j'_!UM$ and $\gamma_j(M,P):j_!M\otimes P\to j_!(M\otimes j^*P)$ be the canonical open comparisons. The open normalization theorem [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] applies both to ring sheaves and to strict ring systems; it supplies these actual maps, their invertibility, and their identity restrictions. In all formulas below insert the canonical pullback/tensor and composition identifications of the statement.

proof.text:
For the square with vertical arrows $p,p'$ and horizontal arrows $v,\bar u$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] with $E=N=j_!M$ and $Q=K$. Its ringed commutation isomorphism is the canonical one $p'^*v^*\cong\bar u^*p^*$: the constant coefficient identifications, or the ring-system identifications at every index, respect the structural ring maps. Its exchange is $e$ because both are the mate of that isomorphism under the specified derived adjunctions. Its projection map $\pi_p(N,K)$ is the counit transpose used in the item, not an arbitrarily chosen projection isomorphism. Consequently, after the indicated target identification, its equality reads
$$e_{N\otimes p^*K}\,G\pi_p(N,K)=\pi_{p'}(HN,GK)(e_N\otimes1).$$
The theorem allows arbitrary objects of the unbounded derived categories and arbitrary commutative ring sheaves, so it applies directly to the ring-system topos too. It requires neither proper base-change invertibility nor a perfectness condition on $K$.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary object $P$ on $\overline X$, the open-factor equality is
$$b_{M\otimes j^*P}\,H\gamma_j(M,P)=\gamma_{j'}(UM,HP)(b_M\otimes1),$$
where the left target is identified using $Uj^*\cong j'^*H$ and the source using the tensor comparison for $H$. To prove it, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] identifies the common source $H(j_!M\otimes P)$, by $\mu_H$, $b_M\otimes1$, and $\gamma_{j'}$, with $j'_!(UM\otimes j'^*HP)$. Thus source and target are in the essential image of the fully faithful $j'_!$, and it suffices to restrict the two maps to $X'$. That theorem says that the restrictions of $b$ and $\gamma$ are the identities under their open unit identifications. The remaining comparisons on both routes identify $U(M\otimes j^*P)$ with $UM\otimes j'^*HP$. They agree directly on the K-flat representatives of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]: in every bidegree both send an inverse-image tensor $m\otimes t$ to the same two inverse-image factors, with $Uj^*t=j'^*Ht$; they preserve bidegrees and the total differential. These equations on tensor generators are local equations of sheaves and descend to the derived category. This also works on the diagram site itself. Full faithfulness now proves the displayed open equality as an equality of system-derived morphisms, without trying to infer it from equality of level evaluations.

proof.text:
Put $N=j_!M$, $W=M\otimes f^*K$, $C=N\otimes p^*K$, and let $\gamma:C\to j_!W$ include $j^*p^*\cong f^*$. Write $\pi=\pi_p(N,K)$, and let $\gamma'$ be the corresponding open tensor map for $j'$ with second input $p'^*GK$. The preceding open equality, applied with $P=p^*K$, includes $Hp^*K\cong p'^*GK$ and therefore says $b_W H\gamma=\gamma'(b_M\otimes1)$. Expand the two definitions in the item and use naturality of $e$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_W\,G\operatorname{PF}_f
 &=R'(b_W)e_{j_!W}\,G(R\gamma)\,G\pi\\
 &=R'(b_W H\gamma)e_C\,G\pi\\
 &=R'\gamma'\,R'(b_M\otimes1)\,\pi_{p'}(HN,GK)(e_N\otimes1)\\
 &=R'\gamma'\,\pi_{p'}(j'_!UM,GK)(R'b_M\,e_N\otimes1)\\
 &=\operatorname{PF}_{f'}(UM,GK)(\beta_M\otimes1).
\end{aligned}$$
The third line uses step 3 and step 2. The fourth uses naturality of the proper projection map in its first input, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied to $b_M:HN\to j'_!UM$; its counit-transpose definition is precisely the present $\pi_{p'}$. The first naturality is that of the mate transformation $e$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. Every displayed target is identified using the same pullback comparisons as in the statement; the open comparison uses $Uj^*p^*\cong j'^*Hp^*\cong j'^*p'^*G$. The last line is the required forward identity. All component maps are natural in $M,K$, so this equality is natural in them.

proof.text: For the final assertion write $B=\beta_M\otimes1$, $C=\beta_{M\otimes f^*K}$, $P=G\operatorname{PF}_f(M,K)$, and $Q=\operatorname{PF}_{f'}(UM,GK)$, with exactly the preceding identifications. Step 4 gives $CP=QB$. Under the isomorphism hypotheses, compose on the left with $Q^{-1}$ and on the right with $P^{-1}C^{-1}$ to obtain $BP^{-1}C^{-1}=Q^{-1}$. Functoriality gives $P^{-1}=v^*(\operatorname{PF}_f(M,K)^{-1})$. This is the displayed inverse identity.
